Formidable

/FOR-mih-duh-bul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Formidable means so impressively powerful, large, or capable that it inspires fear or deep respect.

The climbers stared up at the formidable north face of the mountain, knowing that only a handful of teams had ever reached its summit.

Worked Example

At the regional chess tournament, twelve-year-old Priya faced a formidable opponent: a grandmaster who had not lost a match in three years. She played each move carefully, aware that a single careless exchange would end her run.

The grandmaster's three-year unbeaten record makes him impressively capable and very difficult to overcome, which is exactly what formidable describes. Priya's extreme caution shows the mix of respect and worry that a formidable opponent inspires.

How Formidable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

daunting

daunting: discouragingly difficult to face

intimidating

intimidating: causing nervousness or fear

mighty

mighty: very powerful or strong

Antonyms

weak

weak: lacking power or strength

harmless

harmless: unable to cause fear or damage

How Strong Is It? — challenging → formidable → overwhelming

challenging vs. formidable

challenging vs. formidable: Challenging is milder; a challenging puzzle tests you, but it does not inspire any fear or awe.

overwhelming vs. formidable

overwhelming vs. formidable: Formidable is stronger than challenging because it inspires real dread or deep respect, but overwhelming goes further, describing a force so great it simply cannot be resisted.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — formid

Root — formid: fear, dread (Latin formido)

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: causing, worthy of

Put it together

Put it together: Formidable combines the Latin root formido, meaning fear or dread, with the suffix -able, so the word literally means 'able to cause dread.' Over time it has softened slightly, so today it can also praise something impressively capable.

Use the root in a new word: formidably

Use the root in a new word: formidably: The debate team performed formidably at nationals, sweeping every round they entered.

Word Building

Word Choice

Neutral / slightly formal

Common collocations: a formidable opponent, a formidable task, a formidable reputation. Formidable describes the thing that causes fear or respect, not the person feeling it; a nervous student is fearful, while the exam itself is formidable. Note that formidable is often a compliment: calling someone a formidable negotiator praises their skill.
